- `ex-counting-premeasure-on-the-finite-cofinite-algebra` **[critical]**: I recomputed both branches. Finite `E`: self-cover gives `≤|E|`; `[L1]` disjointifies any cover into `B_k⊆A_k` with `⨆B_k=E`, and `μ₀(B_k)≤μ₀(A_k)` (`|B_k|≤|A_k|` when `A_k` finite, `+∞` when cofinite), so every cover costs `≥Σ|B_k|=|E|`. Infinite `E`: a cofinite member costs `+∞`; a cover by finite members of finite total cardinality has finite union, so cannot cover `E`. Result `|E|`/`+∞` = counting outer measure ✓. The premeasure claim holds because `μ₀` is literally `#|_{𝒜₀}` (every cofinite subset of `ℕ` is infinite).
- `ex-counting-outer-measure-is-metric-on-the-real-line`: positively separated ⟹ disjoint, and `#` is additive on **all** disjoint pairs, so `[F1]` holds a fortiori. Empty-set case handled. Conclusion `every subset is measurable` is stronger than Borel and is licensed by `[L1]`.

**The three `ai-generated` constructions — verified by exhaustive enumeration, no counterexample search needed.**
- `ex-zero-one-outer-measure-on-a-two-point-set`: all four subsets checked; `ℳ={∅,X}` ✓.
- `cex-three-point-outer-measure-has-only-trivial-caratheodory-sets`: `X={1,2,3}`, `μ*(X)=2`, all other nonempty `=1`. Monotone on all five inclusion types ✓. Countably subadditive: a union equal to `X` needs an `X`-member (cost 2) or ≥ 2 nonempty proper members (cost ≥ 2) ✓. Every `E` passes `A=X` (`1+1=2`) ✓, and `A={x,y}` with `x∈E`, `y∉E` gives `1 ≠ 1+1` ✓. The claim it refutes really does need three points — on two points the analogous witness is counting measure, where everything is measurable.
- `cex-two-point-outer-measure-need-not-be-regular`: `μ*(X)=3/2`. Subadditivity ✓ (`2 ≥ 3/2`). `ℳ={∅,X}` since `3/2 ≠ 1+1`. The only measurable superset of a singleton is `X`, and `3/2 ≠ 1`, so no hull exists ✓.

**Metric chain — `d(A,B)>0` is what is used, and the divergent-sum case is closed by hypothesis.**
- `lem-metric-outer-measure-boundary-layer-continuity`: with `C_n = B_{n+1}∖B_n = {x∈A∖F : 1/(n+2) ≤ d(x,F) < 1/(n+1)}`, same-parity `C_i,C_j` (`j≥i+2`) are separated by `d(x,y) ≥ 1/(i+2) − 1/(i+3) > 0` via the 1-Lipschitz property — genuinely **positive**, not merely disjoint, so `[F1]` applies. Peeling the last even annulus from `C_0∪…∪C_{2m-4}` needs `1/(2m-2) − 1/(2m-1) > 0`, which holds; the induction is sound. The divergence case is closed by the Statement's `μ*(A)<+∞`: each parity series is bounded by `μ*(A)`, hence finite, hence its tails vanish, and `(A∖F)∖B_n = ⋃_{k≥n}C_k` is bounded by the two tails, giving `ε/2+ε/2`. Closedness of `F` is what forces `d(x,F)>0` for `x∉F`, and it is used. `F=∅` and `A∖F=∅` are handled explicitly.
- `prop-closed-sets-…`: `d(A∩F, B_n) ≥ 1/(n+1) > 0` because every `y∈A∩F⊆F` has `d(x,y) ≥ d(x,F) ≥ 1/(n+1)` for `x∈B_n`. The `μ*(A)=+∞` branch is separated in 3.1, which is exactly where `[L1]`'s finiteness hypothesis would otherwise be violated.
- `thm-borel-sets-…`: `ℳ` is a σ-algebra containing all closed sets, hence all open sets, hence `ℬ(X)` by minimality; `[F1]` matches `def-borel-sigma-algebra` verbatim.
